messages:
Lia (infra): heads-up — nvme SMART errors on three nodes in spot-gpu-pool-3, noticed after last night's provisioning churn
SRE Oncall Bot: automated alert — nvme SMART threshold breached on node gpu-spot-3a (SMART_WARN = 1)
Lia (infra): logs:
```
[2026-03-18T02:14:22Z] nvme0n1: Media_Error_Count increased to 6
[2026-03-18T02:14:22Z] nvme0n1: temperature 78C
kernel: nvme nvme0: I/O 100ms+ latency spikes
```
Alex W: ok, action: drain and deprovision those nodes, move running batches to overflow-dedicated-1
Maya R: how many nodes affected? cost impact if we move to dedicated overflow?
Lia (infra): 3 nodes: gpu-spot-3a/b/c. We'll replace from the pool but moving running batches will add ~12% infra cost for next 24h (est)
Ben P: FYI runtime: we have several long-lived KV-cache sessions on those nodes; draining will evict caches and increase token cost. Need a smooth handoff.
Cheng: Plan I propose:
1) cordon nodes and mark with tag nvme-wear=high
2) schedule graceful drain with --ignore-daemonsets, --delete-local-data delayed (30m)
3) spin up replacement nodes from warm-reserve (dedicated short-term)
4) run smartctl full-discard+scrub after reboot; if media errors persist -> retire
Commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-spot-3a
kubectl drain gpu-spot-3a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=1800
smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 | egrep 'Media_Error_Count|Temperature'
```
Maya R: +1 to Cheng. Can we limit draining window to business off-peak (03:00–06:00 UTC)?
Alex W: agree. schedule at 03:15 UTC, small batches first to monitor SLO impact. I'll own runtime fallback if costs spike.
Ben P: Will configure fallback policy: route new requests to ded-ovf nodes, keep in-flight up to 2m then failover. Notifying product SLAs.
Lia (infra): tagging the nodes now and creating ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4129 — decommission nvme-warned spot nodes
Ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-4129, assigned Lia (infra)
Cheng: also enabling short-term monitoring: iostat -x 2 and nvme-cli stats collection to the cluster-metrics bucket
Alex W: runbook note: if Media_Error_Count > 10 after scrub -> mark hardware replaceable and set lifecycle retire=ASAP
Maya R: can we automate future detection so we don't have manual panics? i.e., alert on Media_Error_Count delta > 3 in 1h
Cheng: yes, I'll add a metric to node-exporter -> alert rule in prometheus; low-noise threshold and pager only if >3 and temp>70C
Ben P: quick ask — will reboots break pinned model caches? we need to persist or warm them on replacement nodes
Alex W: we'll warm caches via progressive traffic ramp from runtime (5% -> 20% -> 50%) during drain
Lia (infra): scheduling: start 03:15 UTC, 03:15–04:30 target for first node, ramp checks at +10m and +30m
Maya R: :thumbsup: ping me 10m before
Cheng: noted. adding playbook steps to INFRA-4129.
Lia (infra): thanks — will post post-mortem if any unexpected corruption appears. for now: non-urgent but prioritized (P2)
SRE Oncall Bot: incident linked: INFRA-4129 -> monitoring enabled
Alex W: will watch SLO dashboard during window and cancel if error rate > 0.5% above baseline
Lia (infra): final: communicating to workspace ops channel and to customer-support (small rollout note)
Maya R: thanks everyone, good plan
Ben P: good call :thumbsup:
Cheng: starting instrumentation now, will update thread with heartbeat logs
Lia (infra): last note — avoid re-using same spot hardware for training until firmware scrubbed, liaising with cloud vendor
